reproduction.repro_test_code:
import pytest
from datetime import datetime
from dateutil.rrule import rrulestr

def test_byday_mix_union():
    # FR,1FR should give first Fridays each month (this works)
    fr1fr = list(rrulestr("FREQ=MONTHLY;COUNT=5;BYDAY=FR,1FR", dtstart=datetime(2024, 1, 1)))
    assert len(fr1fr) == 5
    assert fr1fr[0] == datetime(2024, 1, 5)
    assert fr1fr[1] == datetime(2024, 2, 2)
    assert fr1fr[2] == datetime(2024, 3, 1)
    assert fr1fr[3] == datetime(2024, 4, 5)
    assert fr1fr[4] == datetime(2024, 5, 3)

    # MO,1FR should give Mondays plus first Fridays (currently broken -> empty)
    mo1fr = list(rrulestr("FREQ=MONTHLY;COUNT=5;BYDAY=MO,1FR", dtstart=datetime(2024, 1, 1)))
    # Expect at least 5 occurrences; first should be Jan 1 (Monday)
    assert len(mo1fr) >= 5
    assert mo1fr[0] == datetime(2024, 1, 1)
    # Ensure we got some Fridays too (e.g., Jan 5 should appear)
    assert datetime(2024, 1, 5) in mo1fr

root_cause: In src/dateutil/rrule.py the _iter method evaluates a day against the plain weekday list (_byweekday) and the ordinal weekday list (_bynweekday) with separate conditions that must both pass: (byweekday and ii.wdaymask[i] not in byweekday) or (ii.nwdaymask and not ii.nwdaymask[i]). This causes a day to be accepted only when it satisfies both lists, i.e., the intersection of plain and ordinal weekdays, instead of the union required by RFC 5545. Consequently, a rule like BYDAY=MO,1FR yields no dates because a day cannot be both a Monday and the first Friday of the same month.
